title: Classic Homemade Pumpkin Pie Recipe
excerpt: There is something wonderfully cozy about a pumpkin pie cooling on the kitchen counter while the house fills with cinnamon and warm autumn spice. This old-fashioned favorite is simple enough for a family baking day and just right for Halloween gatherings, fall suppers, and a generous dollop of whipped cream.

Why You'll Love This Pumpkin Pie Recipe

  • It brings classic fall flavor to the table with pumpkin, cinnamon, and cozy spice.
  • The filling comes together in one mixing bowl with simple pantry-friendly ingredients.
  • A refrigerated crust makes this recipe wonderfully easy for busy family baking days.
  • It is a lovely dessert for Halloween gatherings, Thanksgiving tables, and Sunday suppers.
  • The pie can be made ahead, giving you more time to enjoy your guests.

Ingredients

Gather these simple ingredients before you begin, and you will have everything you need for a smooth, warmly spiced pumpkin pie filling.

  • Refrigerated 9-inch unbaked pie crust - 1 crust
  • Pumpkin puree - 1 can, 15 ounces
  • Evaporated milk - 1 can, 12 ounces
  • Large eggs - 2
  • Granulated sugar - 3/4 cup
  • Pumpkin pie spice - 1 1/2 teaspoons
  • Salt - 1/2 teaspoon
  • Vanilla extract - 1 teaspoon

How to Make Pumpkin Pie Recipe

Plan for about 15 minutes of prep time, 55 minutes of baking, and at least 2 hours of cooling time before slicing. That resting time helps the filling set into neat, creamy pieces.

Step 1: Preheat the Oven

Preheat the oven to 425°F. Let it fully reach temperature while you prepare the crust and filling.

Step 2: Fit the Crust

Fit the pie crust into a 9-inch pie dish. Gently settle it into the corners without stretching the dough.

Step 3: Whisk the Eggs

Whisk the eggs in a large mixing bowl until the yolks and whites are well combined. A smooth egg mixture helps the filling bake evenly.

Step 4: Add the Dry Ingredients

Add the sugar, pumpkin pie spice, and salt to the eggs. Stir until the mixture is evenly blended.

Step 5: Stir in the Pumpkin

Stir the pumpkin puree into the egg mixture. Mix gently until the color and texture look uniform.

Step 6: Add the Evaporated Milk

Pour in the evaporated milk. Stir until it is fully incorporated and the filling looks smooth.

Step 7: Add the Vanilla

Stir in the vanilla extract. This adds a soft, familiar sweetness to the warmly spiced filling.

Step 8: Fill the Crust

Pour the filling into the prepared crust. Place the pie dish on a sturdy baking sheet if you would like extra support when moving it into the oven.

Step 9: Begin Baking

Bake the pie at 425°F for 15 minutes. The higher starting temperature helps the crust begin baking nicely.

Step 10: Reduce the Temperature

Reduce the oven temperature to 350°F. Make the change promptly so the pie can continue baking gently.

Step 11: Finish Baking

Bake the pie for 40 to 50 minutes. The filling should be set around the edges with a slight, gentle wobble in the center.

Step 12: Cool the Pie

Cool the pie on a wire rack for at least 2 hours. Letting it cool completely gives the filling time to set before serving.

Pro Tips for Making Pumpkin Pie Recipe

  • Use pure pumpkin puree rather than pumpkin pie filling so you can control the sugar and spice.
  • Measure the pumpkin pie spice and salt carefully for a balanced, old-fashioned flavor.
  • Do not slice the pie while it is warm, since the filling needs time to set properly.
  • Place the pie on a wire rack after baking so air can circulate around the dish as it cools.
  • For especially tidy slices, chill the cooled pie briefly before serving.

How to Serve Pumpkin Pie Recipe

  • Top each slice with a spoonful of softly whipped cream.
  • Serve the pie with a warm cup of coffee, tea, or apple cider.
  • Add a light dusting of pumpkin pie spice just before serving for a pretty finish.
  • Offer small slices after a family supper or generous slices at a holiday gathering.

Make Ahead and Storage

Storing Leftovers

  • Cover the cooled pie and refrigerate it within 2 hours of baking.
  • Store leftovers in the refrigerator for up to 4 days.
  • Keep slices covered so the crust stays protected from refrigerator odors.

Freezing

  • Cool the pie completely before freezing.
  • Wrap the whole pie or individual slices securely, then place them in a freezer-safe container.
  • Freeze for up to 1 month for the best texture and flavor.
  • Thaw the pie overnight in the refrigerator before serving.

Reheating

  • For a warm slice, place it in a 325°F oven until heated through.
  • Cover the crust edge if needed to prevent excess browning.
  • Individual slices can also be enjoyed chilled or brought to room temperature.

Final Thoughts

This classic pumpkin pie recipe is the kind of comforting dessert that makes an ordinary autumn day feel like a family celebration.

FAQs

Here are a few helpful answers for making and serving this cozy homemade pie.

Can I use homemade pumpkin puree?

Yes, homemade pumpkin puree can work well if it has a smooth texture and is not too watery. Drain excess liquid if needed before measuring.

How do I know when the pumpkin pie is done?

The edges should look set, while the center should have a slight gentle wobble. The filling will continue to set as the pie cools.

Why does pumpkin pie need to cool for 2 hours?

Cooling allows the custard-style filling to finish setting. Slicing too soon can make the center look loose and difficult to serve neatly.

Can I make this pumpkin pie ahead of time?

Yes, you can bake the pie a day ahead and refrigerate it once it has cooled. Bring it out shortly before serving, or serve it chilled with whipped cream.
